data.name: Jnanyan
data.gender_notes: Jnanyan is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the words 'Jnana' (knowledge) and 'Atman' (Self). The name Jnanyan carries the meaning “Wisdom of the Self” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jnanyan usually hope their child will grow to embody wisdom of the self and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Reflects a journey of self-discovery and enlightenment.
data.etymology: Jnanyan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wisdom of the Self.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jnanyan total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jnanyan is a noble and revered one in Hindu culture, often associated with those who are deeply knowledgeable in various domains, be it scriptures, literature, or other areas of expertise. These individuals are respected and held in high esteem within their communities for their dedication to learning and the sharing of wisdom with others.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper level, the name Jnanyan carries profound spiritual significance as it represents the quest for self-knowledge and the pursuit of enlightenment or 'Jnana' - the direct realization of one's true nature as the all-pervading consciousness or 'Atman'. The name serves as a daily reminder and inspiration for the bearer to constantly deepen their understanding of the Self and the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Jnanyan signifies one who is deeply wise and knowledgeable. It symbolizes the pursuit of spiritual knowledge and the realization of truth through self-study and inner reflection. The embodiment of a seeker on the path of enlightenment.
